**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The agreement imposes no take-or-pay exposure on AbbVie, satisfying the MINCOMMIT preferred position ("no minimum commitment").

What I checked and found:

- **No minimum/volume construct anywhere.** Searches for "minimum", "purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", and "quantities" surfaced nothing relevant. The only "minimum" hits are mutual insurance limits in Section 11.6; the only "purchase" hit is a Distributor definition carve-out in Article 5.
- **Section 4.5.1 is a right, not an obligation.** AbbVie has the *sole right, at its expense*, to Manufacture and supply commercial product. There is no obligation to source volumes from Harpoon, so no supply-side commitment can arise.
- **Payment structure is event-based, not volume-based.** Section 6.1 is a $30M upfront; Sections 6.2/6.3 are development, regulatory and sales milestones, plus royalties on Net Sales. These are triggered by achievement or actual sales — never by failure to take volume, which is the hallmark of take-or-pay.
- **Manufacturing Technology Transfer (4.5.2–4.5.3) runs in our favour** (Harpoon must transfer know-how on our request, at its own expense pre-exercise), so per the direction rule I did not flag it.

Deliberate non-flags, per the playbook's anti-double-counting instruction: the Commercially Reasonable Efforts diligence obligations (Sections 3 and 4.2) and the milestone schedule are genuine obligations on us, but they are separate commercial terms belonging to other rules — they are not volume commitments and would be double-flagged if raised here. Section 4.2 also already includes a good-faith discussion mechanic rather than an automatic penalty.

One note for the record rather than a deviation: several milestone amounts and the Section 4.2 diligence provisos are redacted as `[***]`, so I could not confirm their quantum. Nothing in the visible structure suggests a volume commitment hiding there, but if the unredacted milestone schedule contains a sales-volume trigger with a make-whole payment, that would warrant a fresh look under this rule.
